title: Picard descended fibre coefficient is trivial
statement: Let f:X to S be a scheme morphism whose tensor-pullback structure adjunction unit is an isomorphism after every base change. Let L be invertible on X, let s be a point of S, and suppose L_s is isomorphic to the pullback of a finite locally free N on Spec kappa(s). Then L_s is isomorphic to the structure module on X_s. The universal structure-unit condition and tensor pullback are [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction, def-pc-module-pullback], invertibility is [def-sc-invertible-module], and finite local freeness is [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. No derived model, target family, basis, flatness or properness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BF2, displayed fibre-coefficient identification; Tag 0BDP, fibrewise descent criterion and field rank-one consequence; parent proof step 2

proof.text: At Spec kappa(s), an empty source fibre would make every module on the fibre zero (Modules.isZero_of_isEmpty). Additive pushforward preserves zero objects. The assumed invertible adjunction unit would make the nonzero field-spectrum structure module zero (Modules.not_isZero_unit), a contradiction. Thus X_s is nonempty.

Identify tensor pullback with ordinary module pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints. Ordinary pullback preserves invertibility. Transport it through the descent isomorphism to the pullback of N. Apply field pullback rank-one triviality on the nonempty source fibre, obtaining N isomorphic to the field structure module.
Apply tensor pullback to the trivialization of N, compose with the descent isomorphism, and use the pullback structure-unit isomorphism. This yields the asserted trivialization of L_s.
